title: WPMS/781/2010 of SMT SUREN LATA Vs SMT BIMLA

paras.text:
IN THE COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 781 of 2010 (M/S)
Smt Suren Lata ...Petitioner
Versus
Smt. Bimla W/o Sri Satveer ... Respondent
Present:
Mr. Arvind Kumar Sharma, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Sanjay Kumar, Advocate for the respondent.
Dated: 14th December, 2017
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
In the instant writ petition, the petitioner has
questioned the validity orders dated 21st May, 2005, passed
by the Assistant Settlement Officer, Consolidation and the
order dated 15th May, 2010, passed by the Deputy Director of
Consolidation, Haridwar.
The father-in-law of the petitioner and respondent, Mr.
Jaiman is said to have executed a will on 16th September,
2002 in relation to the estates belonging to him. Based on the
will, proceedings under Section 12 was drawn by the present
petitioner for getting herself recorded in the revenue records
after deletion of name of Jaiman, her father-in-law. In the
proceedings thus initiated under Section 12, the statement
was recorded of the respondent Smt. Bimla on 17th June, 2003
and that of the present writ petitioner on the same day and,
thereafter, the Consolidation Officer passed an order in Case
No. 124, whereby, both petitioner and respondent were
directed to be recorded in revenue records based on the will
dated 16th September, 2002.
On account of the fact that while the said entry was
being made in pursuance to the order dated 6th September,

2
2003, as it was not settling the share, hence, a fresh order was
passed, by virtue of which, both petitioner and respondent
were allocated 1⁄2 share each, based on the order passed by
the Consolidation Officer on 13th May, 2005, in Appeal No.
764 of 2005, Smt. Bimla Vs. Smt. Suren Lata.
The respondent contending herself to be aggrieved by
the order passed by the Consolidation Officer under Section
12, though, since by order of Consoidation Officer, both were
recorded against equal share, there ought to be any
grievance left with the respondent yet, she preferred an
appeal being Appeal No. 767 of 2005, Bimla Vs. Smt. Suren
Lata, after a lapse of two years alongwith the delay
condonation application.
The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner
is that on institution of the appeal, the ordersheet reveals
that as a matter of fact no notices were never issued to the
present petitioner nor the ordersheet contains any direction
given by the Court to the appellant, i.e. respondent, herein,
to take steps for serving the respondent in the appeal, i.e. the
petitioner before this Court.
Within one month from the date of institution of the
appeal, by the order dated 21st May, 2005, the Assistant
Settlement Officer, Consolidation by recording a perverse
finding that he has heard the petitioner proceeded to pass an
order on 21st May, 2005, impugned in the writ petition,
whereby, the order dated 6th September, 2003, directing the
petitioner and respondent to be recorded in equal based on
the will of Jaiman was set aside. Against the said order, the
petitioner preferred a revision, the revision too has been
dismissed by the order dated 15th May, 2010.

3
Both the Courts below had proceeded on a premise as
if at the time when the appeal preferred by the respondent
and when it was being decided, the petitioner was being
represented and that is why a finding has been recorded by
the Appellate Court as under:-
"izfr mRrjnkrk dh vksj ls vihykUV ds dFku dk dk sb Z
fojks/k ugh fd;k x;k cfYd pd la0&83 dk foHkktu vihykUV dh
ekax ds vu qlkj fd;s tku s gsr w viuh lgefr nh x;h gSA"
This finding, apparently, from the ordersheet is
perverse. This Court reiterates the fact that when no notices
were sent, either on Section 5 application or on the appeal,
and when there was no disposal of Section 5 Application,
when the ordersheet does not reflect that any steps were
taken by the respondent for effecting the service on the
present petitioner, the order dated 21st May, 2005, itself,
would be perverse.
The learned counsel for the respondent submits that by
setting aside the order dated 6th May, 2003, by the Appellate
Court by the impugned order dated 21st May, 2005, it was
not prejudicing the right of the present petitioner. This is not
the stage, when the said fact could be scrutinized by this
Court, for the reason, whether a party to a lis is affected or
not affected, the determination of said question would only
arise when the party is noticed, he puts in appearance and
raises his or her rival claim. The inferences in legal
proceedings about the prejudice caused by the impugned
orders cannot be hypothetically determined without an
opportunity.
The learned counsel for the petitioner further submits
that there is an endorsement made by the petitioner in the
order dated 13th May, 2005. As already submitted that since

4
the petitioner was not noticed, there was no occasion for her
to make an endorsement as to in what manner and how the
order bears the endorsement is a mystry unsolved.
Since all these questions are required to be scrutinized
by the Appellate Court, I quash the order dated 15th May,
2010, passed by the Deputy Director, Consolidation and 21st
May, 2005, passed by the Assistant Settlement Officer,
Consolidation and remit the matter to the Court of Assistant
Settlement Officer Consolidation to decide the appeal afresh
after providing an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner.
The writ petition is allowed.
No order as to costs.
Till the appeal is decided, coupled with the fact right of
both the parties would be conferred by decision of will, till
any decision is arrived at, they will not create third party
interest during the pendency of the appeal.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
14.12.2017
Shiv
